paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: the LORD is not a god you can handle. The Philistines tried to figure Him out with a test, two cows and a cart, and the cows headed straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh, never straying to the right or to the left (1 Samuel 6:12). Their own priests and diviners had even pointed back to Egypt and asked why they would harden their hearts like Pharaoh (1 Samuel 6:6). Even people who don't know Him can see His hand when He moves, and the wise thing is to give Him glory (1 Samuel 6:5).

Then the people of Beth-shemesh show us the other side. They were overjoyed to see the ark (1 Samuel 6:13), and then God struck down seventy men because they looked inside the ark of the LORD (1 Samuel 6:19). I think that part is heavy, and it should be. Their own question says it best: "Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God?" (1 Samuel 6:20).

So what do we do with that, baker? We take God seriously and we come to Him on His terms, not ours. Joy and reverence belong together, like a warm oven and a good pair of mitts. We can't box Him up, test Him or peek inside, but we can listen to Him, and that's why I keep my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper. And this story is far from done.
